title: Leaderboard: K-th Place
statement:
Players finish an arcade game one after another, and each gets a score. The game has a prize for the player in **k-th place**, so after every new score the screen shows the k-th highest score so far (counting equal scores separately).

If fewer than k scores have been recorded, the screen shows -1.

Print what the screen shows after each of the **q** scores.
input:
The first line contains two integers **k** and **q**.

The second line contains q integers: the scores in the order they arrive.
output: Print q integers on one line separated by spaces: the value on the screen after each score.

samples.explanation: After 10, 40, 20 the third best is 10. After 30 arrives the top three are 40, 30, 20, so 20 is shown. After the second 40 the top three are 40, 40, 30.

hints: Sorting all scores after every new one is too slow.
You only need the best k scores. Keep them in a min-heap: its top is the k-th highest score. When a new score is bigger than the top, replace the top.
editorial:
Keep a min-heap with at most k elements: the k best scores so far. For a new score x: if the heap has fewer than k elements, push x; otherwise, if x is greater than the smallest element (the top), pop the top and push x. After processing, if the heap has k elements its top is the k-th highest score, otherwise print -1. In C++ use `priority_queue<int, vector<int>, greater<int>>`, in Python `heapq`.

Complexity: O(q log k).
